title: SAP finance: charts of accounts and G/L accounts, customer and supplier open items, cost and profit centers, and how journal lines point at them
status_note: Every table, key and relationship below is taken from public documentation and written in our own words. None of it has been checked against an SAP system by this project; validate_plan checks it against your rows. A pack is a sourced suggestion, not proof. Builds on the accounting_document module (BKPF, BSEG, ACDOCA).

tables.name: SKA1
tables.en: G/L account, chart of accounts segment
tables.note: An account number means something only within its chart of accounts (KTOPL).

tables.name: SKB1
tables.note: Has no chart of accounts column: the chart comes from the company code (T001.KTOPL).

tables.name: BSID
tables.note: Copies of customer lines of BSEG that are still open; cleared ones move to BSAD. Marked ECC: in S/4HANA it is read through a compatibility view, not asserted here.

tables.name: CSKS
tables.note: Time-dependent: one row per validity period, ending at DATBI. A cost center number alone matches every period.

tables.name: CEPC
tables.note: Time-dependent like CSKS; the controlling area is the last key column.

relationships.condition: Customer lines only; other lines leave KUNNR empty.
Supplier lines only; other lines leave LIFNR empty.
Customer lines only; other lines leave KUNNR empty.
Supplier lines only; other lines leave LIFNR empty.
CSKS is time-dependent: the line's posting date (BUDAT) must fall in the cost center's validity period (up to DATBI). An equality join on the number alone matches every period.
CEPC is time-dependent; pick the period by posting date, and the controlling area as well.

traps.title: Open items are copies of journal lines
traps.text: BSID, BSAD, BSIK and BSAK hold copies of customer and supplier lines of BSEG, split by open and cleared. Adding them to BSEG (or ACDOCA) counts the same posting twice, and open plus cleared together are all items: use one source per question. An item moves from the open to the cleared table when it is cleared, so a delta load on one table alone sees it disappear.

traps.title: Cost and profit centers have validity periods
traps.text: CSKS and CEPC have DATBI (valid to) in the key: one cost center number has a row per period. Joining a journal line on the number alone multiplies it by the number of periods; pick the period in which the posting date falls. The pack lists these links but does not apply them as relationships.

traps.title: An account number needs its chart of accounts
traps.text: SAKNR is unique only within a chart of accounts (KTOPL), and SKB1 and journal lines carry no KTOPL: it comes from the company code, T001.KTOPL. Join SKA1 (for the account's name) through T001, not on SAKNR alone.

traps.title: Debit and credit
traps.text: BSEG and the open-item tables store amounts without a sign and say debit or credit in SHKZG; ACDOCA stores signed amounts. A sum over ECC lines without SHKZG adds credits as debits.

traps.title: Special G/L transactions in the open items
traps.text: UMSKZ marks down payments, guarantees and other special G/L transactions in the open-item tables. A receivables total usually leaves them out or shows them apart.
